# wallix.bastion.authorization

Manage authorizations on a WALLIX Bastion — module

*Added in version 1.0.0 of `wallix.bastion`.*

## Synopsis

- Create, update or delete an authorization on a WALLIX Bastion.
- An authorization gives the members of a user group access to the targets of a target group (sessions, password retrieval, or both), optionally subject to approval.
- Equivalent of the `wallix-bastion_authorization` Terraform resource.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Comments |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="parameter-active-quorum"></a>**active_quorum** | `int` | Number of approvals needed during the timeframes of the user group.<br>The Bastion sets it to `-1` when approval is not required. |
| <a id="parameter-api-version"></a>**api_version** | `str` | Version of the Bastion REST API to use, `v3.8` or `v3.12`.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_API_VERSION` environment variable is used, then `v3.12`. |
| <a id="parameter-approval-required"></a>**approval_required** | `bool` | Whether access requires the approval of an [`approvers`](#parameter-approvers) member.<br>Setting it to `false` makes the Bastion reset [`approvers`](#parameter-approvers), [`active_quorum`](#parameter-active-quorum) and [`inactive_quorum`](#parameter-inactive-quorum); do not set those options together with [`approval_required=false`](#parameter-approval-required). |
| <a id="parameter-approval-timeout"></a>**approval_timeout** | `int` | Minutes an approval request stays valid. `0` means no timeout. |
| <a id="parameter-approvers"></a>**approvers** | `list / elements=str` | Names of the user groups whose members can approve access requests. Order does not matter.<br>When set, replaces all the approvers of the authorization. |
| <a id="parameter-authorization-name"></a>**authorization_name** | `str` / required | Name of the authorization. Identifies the authorization on the Bastion. |
| <a id="parameter-authorize-password-retrieval"></a>**authorize_password_retrieval** | `bool` | Whether members can check out the passwords of the target group's password retrieval accounts.<br>The Bastion enables it when it is not set on creation; set it to `false` to grant sessions only. |
| <a id="parameter-authorize-session-sharing"></a>**authorize_session_sharing** | `bool` | Whether members can invite other users to their sessions. |
| <a id="parameter-authorize-sessions"></a>**authorize_sessions** | `bool` | Whether members can open sessions on the targets. Requires [`subprotocols`](#parameter-subprotocols).<br>The Bastion enables it when it is not set on creation. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-host"></a>**bastion_host** | `str` | Hostname or IP address of the WALLIX Bastion.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_HOST` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-password"></a>**bastion_password** | `str` | Password of [`bastion_user`](#parameter-bastion-user).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_PASSWORD` environment variable is used.<br>One of [`bastion_password`](#parameter-bastion-password) or [`bastion_token`](#parameter-bastion-token) is required. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-port"></a>**bastion_port** | `int` | HTTPS port of the WALLIX Bastion API.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_PORT` environment variable is used, then `443`. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-timeout"></a>**bastion_timeout** | `int` | Timeout in seconds of each HTTP request to the Bastion API.<br><br>Default: `30` |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-token"></a>**bastion_token** | `str` | API key of [`bastion_user`](#parameter-bastion-user). Takes precedence over [`bastion_password`](#parameter-bastion-password).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_TOKEN` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-user"></a>**bastion_user** | `str` | User to authenticate with. With [`bastion_token`](#parameter-bastion-token), the user the API key belongs to.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_USER` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-csrf-enabled"></a>**csrf_enabled** | `bool` | Send the CSRF token the Bastion issues at login (Bastion 12.0.3 and later).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_CSRF_ENABLED` environment variable is used, then `true`. |
| <a id="parameter-description"></a>**description** | `str` | Description of the authorization. |
| <a id="parameter-has-comment"></a>**has_comment** | `bool` | Whether users can add a comment to their approval request. |
| <a id="parameter-has-ticket"></a>**has_ticket** | `bool` | Whether users can add a ticket number to their approval request. |
| <a id="parameter-inactive-quorum"></a>**inactive_quorum** | `int` | Number of approvals needed outside the timeframes of the user group, same values as [`active_quorum`](#parameter-active-quorum). |
| <a id="parameter-is-critical"></a>**is_critical** | `bool` | Whether sessions opened through this authorization are flagged as critical. |
| <a id="parameter-is-recorded"></a>**is_recorded** | `bool` | Whether sessions opened through this authorization are recorded. |
| <a id="parameter-mandatory-comment"></a>**mandatory_comment** | `bool` | Whether the comment is mandatory. |
| <a id="parameter-mandatory-ticket"></a>**mandatory_ticket** | `bool` | Whether the ticket number is mandatory. |
| <a id="parameter-session-sharing-mode"></a>**session_sharing_mode** | `str` | What invited users can do in a shared session.<br><br>Choices: `view_only`, `view_control` |
| <a id="parameter-single-connection"></a>**single_connection** | `bool` | Whether an approval allows a single connection only. |
| <a id="parameter-state"></a>**state** | `str` | Whether the authorization should exist.<br><br>Choices: `present` (default), `absent` |
| <a id="parameter-subprotocols"></a>**subprotocols** | `list / elements=str` | Subprotocols allowed in sessions, for example `SSH_SHELL_SESSION`, `SSH_SCP_UP`, `SFTP_SESSION`, `RDP` or `RDP_CLIPBOARD_UP`. Order does not matter.<br>When set, replaces all the subprotocols of the authorization. The Bastion requires at least one, even when sessions are not authorized, so it cannot be emptied once set. |
| <a id="parameter-target-group"></a>**target_group** | `str` | Name of the target group the authorization gives access to.<br>Required when the authorization does not exist yet and [`state=present`](#parameter-state).<br>Cannot be changed once the authorization exists; delete and recreate it instead. |
| <a id="parameter-user-group"></a>**user_group** | `str` | Name of the user group the authorization applies to.<br>Required when the authorization does not exist yet and [`state=present`](#parameter-state).<br>Cannot be changed once the authorization exists; delete and recreate it instead.<br>The Bastion allows one authorization per pair of user group and target group. |
| <a id="parameter-validate-certs"></a>**validate_certs** | `bool` | Whether to validate the Bastion's TLS certificate.<br>Only disable this for test instances with self-signed certificates.<br>If not set, `WALLIX_BASTION_VALIDATE_CERTS` is used, then the inverse of `WALLIX_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY`, then `true`. |

## Attributes

| Attribute | Support | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **check_mode** | full | Can run in check_mode and return changed status prediction without modifying target. |
| **diff_mode** | full | Will return details on what has changed (or possibly needs changing in check_mode), when in diff mode. |

## Notes

- Options left unset keep their current value on the Bastion.
- The authorization is looked up by [`authorization_name`](#parameter-authorization-name), so it cannot be renamed with this module.
- The environment variables are the ones of the `wallix/wallix-bastion` Terraform provider, so one shell configuration serves both tools.
- Set the connection options once per play with `module_defaults` and the `group/wallix.bastion.bastion` action group.
- These modules call the Bastion API from the host they run on; use them with `delegate_to` or on a play targeting `localhost`.

## Examples

```yaml
- name: Let Linux administrators open SSH sessions on the Linux servers
  wallix.bastion.authorization:
    authorization_name: linux-admins-on-linux-servers
    user_group: linux-admins
    target_group: linux-servers
    authorize_sessions: true
    authorize_password_retrieval: false
    subprotocols: [SSH_SHELL_SESSION, SSH_SCP_UP, SSH_SCP_DOWN]
    is_recorded: true

- name: Require the approval of a security officer
  wallix.bastion.authorization:
    authorization_name: linux-admins-on-linux-servers
    approval_required: true
    approvers: [security-officers]
    active_quorum: 1
    inactive_quorum: 1
    has_comment: true
    mandatory_comment: true

- name: Remove an authorization
  wallix.bastion.authorization:
    authorization_name: linux-admins-on-linux-servers
    state: absent
```

## Return values

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="return-authorization"></a>**authorization** | `dict` | The authorization as returned by the Bastion API after the change.<br>In check mode, the expected authorization. `null` when [`state=absent`](#parameter-state).<br><br>Returned: always<br><br>Sample: see [below](#sample-authorization) |
| <a id="return-changed-fields"></a>**changed_fields** | `list / elements=str` | Options that differed from the Bastion and were updated.<br><br>Returned: when the authorization already existed and [`state=present`](#parameter-state)<br><br>Sample: `["subprotocols"]` |

### Sample of `authorization`

```yaml
active_quorum: -1
approval_required: false

approvers: []
authorization_name: linux-admins-on-linux-servers
authorize_password_retrieval: false
authorize_session_sharing: false
authorize_sessions: true
description: ''
has_comment: false
has_ticket: false
id: 1a0f6ea31fcb3e15005056b66c8b
inactive_quorum: -1
is_critical: false
is_recorded: true
mandatory_comment: false
mandatory_ticket: false
session_sharing_mode: null
single_connection: false
subprotocols:
- SSH_SHELL_SESSION
- SSH_SCP_UP
- SSH_SCP_DOWN
target_group: linux-servers
url: https://bastion.example.com/api/v3.12/authorizations/1a0f6ea31fcb3e15005056b66c8b
user_group: linux-admins
```
